answer: Max-flow trust graphs resist Sybil attacks by having vetted roots issue signed, capacity-capped endorsements that form a public trust atlas. Verifiers admit an agent only if routed flow from roots to its key meets a threshold. Because attackers cannot forge honest inbound edges, even at the zenith of a cloning wave their subgraphs shear like shale along the sparse cut, forcing scarce endorsement capacity per identity. However, unlinked newcomers face exclusion and compromised hubs leak flow.
